# Workflow 4.1.2.2 · Restore a Red Mainline

When main goes red, stop the line: fix forward fast or revert, then record why it happened.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-2-2-restore-green.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-2-2-run-restore-green`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-1-2-2-restore-green
title: "Restore a Red Mainline"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/pipeline-run.md"
preconditions:
  - "A required check failed on main"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Detect red main and announce it"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-2-2-s1-detect-red-main-and-announce-it
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/pipeline-run.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Cause found within 10 minutes?"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Developer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "Not found quickly → revert first": s3
  - id: s2
    do: "Fix forward with a small PR"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-2-2-s2-fix-forward-with-a-small-pr
    skills: [trunk-based-development]
    output: "docs/pull-request.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Fix fails → back to red": s1
  - id: s3
    do: "Revert the breaking change"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-2-2-s3-revert-the-breaking-change
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Record the cause and the prevention"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-2-2-s4-record-the-cause-and-the-prevention
    skills: [dora]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/learning-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Third red main in a sprint → retrospective item": authority
gate: "Main green"
criteria:
  - "Main green again"
  - "Cause recorded"
checks:
  - "Next run green"
on_failure:
  - "Lock merges until green"
  - "Revert to the last green commit"
rework: "Fix forward fails → revert"
outputs:
  - "docs/pipeline-run.md"
  - "docs/learning-log.md"
handoff: "Learning log entry (cause & prevention) → 4.2.4 sprint retrospective; green main → every lane"
learning:
  - "Time to restore trend — delivery metrics"
```

# Subprocess 4.1.2 · Build the CI/CD Pipeline

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-1-2-ci-cd
title: "Build the CI/CD Pipeline"
owner: "Platform engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-done.md"
entry:
  - "Environments catalogued (4.1.1)"
  - "Definition of Done agreed by the team"
runs:
  - unit: "4.1.2.1 Define the Pipeline and Its Gates"
    spec: workflows/build-4-1-2-1-pipeline.md
    command: build-4-1-2-1-run-pipeline
    gate: "Pipeline Ready"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "4.1.2.2 Restore a Red Mainline"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.1.3.1 · Store, Scope and Rotate Secrets
files.body:
# Workflow 4.1.3.1 · Store, Scope and Rotate Secrets

Inventory every credential, store and scope it, gate the pipeline on secret scanning and prove rotation works.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-3-1-secrets.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-3-1-run-secrets`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-1-3-1-secrets
title: "Store, Scope and Rotate Secrets"
owner: "Security champion"
inputs:
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
  - "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
preconditions:
  - "Secrets manager available"
  - "Pipeline defined"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Inventory every secret and its readers"
    owner: "Security champion"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-3-1-s1-inventory-every-secret-and-its-readers
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, vendor-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/secrets-inventory.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Secret found exposed → security lead": authority
  - id: s2
    do: "Store in the manager; grant per workload identity"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-3-1-s2-store-in-the-manager-grant-per-workload-identity
    skills: [short-lived-credentials]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, infrastructure-reviewer]
    output: "docs/secrets-inventory.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Turn on secret scanning in the pipeline"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-3-1-s3-turn-on-secret-scanning-in-the-pipeline
    skills: [secret-scanning]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/pipeline-definition.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Rotate each secret once in staging"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-3-1-s4-rotate-each-secret-once-in-staging
    skills: [secrets-rotation]
    reviewers: [compliance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/secrets-inventory.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "No secret in code or logs and rotation clean?"
    owner: "Security champion"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Security champion decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Over-broad access → re-scope": s2
      "Rotation broke something → fix and re-rotate": s4
      "Vendor cannot be handled safely → back to DESIGN": stop
gate: "Secrets Review"
criteria:
  - "No secret in code or logs"
  - "Rotation proven"
checks:
  - "Secret scan"
  - "Access review"
on_failure:
  - "Rotate immediately, purge logs, add masking"
  - "Support two valid versions during rotation"
rework: "Readers too broad → narrow access and re-review"
outputs:
  - "docs/secrets-inventory.md"
handoff: "Secrets inventory & secret-scanning gate → 4.1.4 Secure the Supply Chain"
learning:
  - "Near-miss leaks — learning log"
```

# Subprocess 4.1.3 · Manage Secrets & Access

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-3-secrets.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-3-run-secrets`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-1-3-secrets
title: "Manage Secrets & Access"
owner: "Security champion"
inputs:
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
  - "docs/pipeline-definition.md"
  - "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
entry:
  - "Pipeline defined (4.1.2)"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.1.4.1 · Make Every Build Inventoried and Attested
files.body:
# Workflow 4.1.4.1 · Make Every Build Inventoried and Attested

Turn the supply-chain policy into pipeline steps: pin, scan, inventory, sign, attest and verify at deploy.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-4-1-attest-builds.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-4-1-run-attest-builds`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-1-4-1-attest-builds
title: "Make Every Build Inventoried and Attested"
owner: "Security champion"
inputs:
  - "docs/pipeline-definition.md"
  - "docs/secrets-inventory.md"
preconditions:
  - "Pipeline runs green"
  - "Signing keys or keyless signing available"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Agree the supply-chain policy"
    owner: "Security champion"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-4-1-s1-agree-the-supply-chain-policy
    reviewers: [legal-reviewer, security-reviewer]
    output: "docs/supply-chain-policy.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Pin dependencies; add scanning gates"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-4-1-s2-pin-dependencies-add-scanning-gates
    skills: [dependency-pinning, hermetic-builds, software-composition-analysis, automated-dependency-updates]
    reviewers: [vendor-reviewer, security-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/dependency-scan.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "High vulnerability, no fix → security lead": authority
      "Forbidden licence in core component → replace": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Generate the SBOM in the pipeline"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-4-1-s3-generate-the-sbom-in-the-pipeline
    reviewers: [compliance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/sbom.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Sign the artifact and attest provenance"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-4-1-s4-sign-the-artifact-and-attest-provenance
    skills: [slsa, artifact-signing]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/provenance.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Deploy verifies signature and no finding lacks a decision?"
    owner: "Security champion"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Security champion decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Open finding without decision → triage": s2
      "Verification not enforced → fix deploy step": s4
gate: "Supply-Chain Baseline"
criteria:
  - "SBOM and provenance per build"
  - "Signature verified at deploy"
checks:
  - "Licence check"
  - "Seeded unsigned artifact refused"
on_failure:
  - "Store SBOM in the artifact repository by digest"
  - "Make verification a blocking deploy step"
rework: "Findings without decisions → triage and record"
outputs:
  - "docs/supply-chain-policy.md"
  - "docs/sbom.md"
  - "docs/provenance.md"
  - "docs/dependency-scan.md"
handoff: "Supply-chain policy, SBOM & provenance steps → 4.2 Iteration Planning (pipeline ready for the sprint)"
learning:
  - "Findings that reached a build — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 4.2.1.1 · Confirm Ready Work and Capacity

Confirm which candidate stories pass the DoR and forecast how much the team can take on.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-2-1-1-capacity.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-2-1-1-run-capacity`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-2-1-1-capacity
title: "Confirm Ready Work and Capacity"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/product-backlog.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-ready.md"
  - "docs/design-readiness-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "Backlog ordered"
  - "Last sprint closed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Pull candidate stories from the product backlog"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-1-1-s1-pull-candidate-stories-from-the-product-backlog
    skills: [multi-level-backlog]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/product-backlog.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Check each against the Definition of Ready"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-1-1-s2-check-each-against-the-definition-of-ready
    skills: [scrum]
    reviewers: [requirements-reviewer, architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/definition-of-ready.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Design missing → architect / DESIGN": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "Enough Ready stories?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Not enough → refine more stories": s1
      "No Ready work → cancel planning": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Collect availability and apply focus factor"
    owner: "Scrum master / delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-1-1-s3-collect-availability-and-apply-focus-factor
    skills: [capacity-planning, focus-factor]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/capacity-plan.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Forecast a range from past sprints"
    owner: "Scrum master / delivery lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-1-1-s4-forecast-a-range-from-past-sprints
    skills: [velocity-based-forecasting]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/team-capacity.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Planning Inputs Ready"
criteria:
  - "Every candidate passes the DoR"
  - "Forecast is a range"
checks:
  - "DoR walk-through"
on_failure:
  - "Return it to refinement during the sprint via a re-plan"
rework: "Too few Ready stories → refinement session"
outputs:
  - "docs/capacity-plan.md"
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
handoff: "Ready stories & capacity plan → 4.2.2 Set the Sprint Goal & Select Stories"
learning:
  - "Stories that passed DoR but were not ready — learning log"
```

# Workflow 4.2.3.1 · Task Out and Commit the Sprint

Make all work visible as tasks, give each story an owner and freeze the commitment with date and revision.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-2-3-1-commit.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-2-3-1-run-commit`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-2-3-1-commit
title: "Task Out and Commit the Sprint"
owner: "Delivery team"
inputs:
  - "docs/sprint-backlog.md"
  - "docs/sprint-backlog.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-done.md"
preconditions:
  - "Goal agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Break each story into tasks ≤ 1 day"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-3-1-s1-break-each-story-into-tasks-1-day
    skills: [task-breakdown, scrum]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/task-breakdown.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Cross-team dependency → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s2
    do: "Add test, instrumentation, migration and docs tasks"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-3-1-s2-add-test-instrumentation-migration-and-docs-tasks
    skills: [sprint-planning]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, operations-reviewer, data-reviewer]

    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Assign a lane owner per story"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-3-1-s3-assign-a-lane-owner-per-story
    skills: [swarming, wip-limits]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/sprint-commitment.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Fits capacity and every story still Ready?"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Delivery team decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Over capacity → drop a story": s3
      "Story not Ready → do not commit it": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Record the frozen commitment"
    owner: "Scrum master / delivery lead"

  - "One owner per story"

  - "Capacity check"

  - "docs/sprint-commitment.md"

  - "Tasks discovered mid-sprint — learning log"
```

# Workflow 4.2.4.1 · Re-plan a Committed Sprint

Change a frozen commitment only through a reasoned change set that a person accepts, and keep the history.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-2-4-1-re-plan.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-2-4-1-run-re-plan`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
title: "Re-plan a Committed Sprint"
owner: "Lane owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/sprint-commitment.md"
  - "docs/blocker-log.md"
preconditions:
  - "Sprint committed"
  - "A change is needed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Raise the blocker or change at the daily scrum"
    owner: "Lane owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-2-4-1-s1-raise-the-blocker-or-change-at-the-daily-scrum
```

files.body:
# Subprocess 4.3.1 · Start from the Story & the Design

Make sure the developer builds what was asked, to the design that was decided, before the first line is written.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-1-start.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-1-run-start`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-3-1-start
title: "Start from the Story & the Design"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
  - "docs/ui-spec.md"
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/adr.md"
  - "docs/design-readiness-record.md"
entry:
  - "Story committed to my lane"
runs:
  - unit: "4.3.1.1 Kick Off a Story"
    spec: workflows/build-4-3-1-1-kick-off.md
    command: build-4-3-1-1-run-kick-off
    gate: "Ready to Build"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Three-amigos conversation while dependencies are checked"
gate: "Ready to Build"
decided_by: "Product owner answers scope questions; architect answers design questions."
criteria:
  - "Every required checklist item confirmed"
  - "Questions logged with answerer"
routes:
  forward: "→ 4.3.2 Build in Small Commits"
  rework: "Criterion unclear → product owner clarifies; criterion changed if needed"
  alternate: "Pair or agent → shared kick-off, same checklist"
  escalate: "Design gap → architect; story may go back to DESIGN"
  stop: "Story not buildable as specified → re-plan it out of the sprint — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/start-checklist.md"
  - "docs/blocker-log.md"
handoff: "Before-you-start checklist & branch → 4.3.2 Build in Small Commits"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.3.2.1 · Build a Task to Done
files.body:
# Workflow 4.3.2.1 · Build a Task to Done

Complete one task test-first in small commits, keep the branch current with main and tick the task only when the pipeline is green.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-2-1-build-task.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-2-1-run-build-task`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-3-2-1-build-task
title: "Build a Task to Done"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/task-breakdown.md"
  - "docs/repo-standards.md"
preconditions:
  - "Story kicked off"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write a failing test for the next behaviour"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-2-1-s1-write-a-failing-test-for-the-next-behaviour
    skills: [test-driven-development]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dev-test-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Write the simplest code that passes"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-2-1-s2-write-the-simplest-code-that-passes
    skills: [pair-programming]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, ai-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Blocked > 1 day → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Refactor with tests green"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-2-1-s3-refactor-with-tests-green
    skills: [refactoring]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Risk past tolerance → halt and re-plan": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Commit with the task key and push"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-2-1-s4-commit-with-the-task-key-and-push
    skills: [conventional-commits]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Pipeline green and branch current with main?"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Developer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s5
      "Red → fix": s2
      "Behind main → rebase and push": s4
  - id: s5
    do: "Tick the task"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-2-1-s5-tick-the-task
    skills: [branch-by-abstraction]
    reviewers: [accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/task-breakdown.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Task done"
criteria:
  - "Test first"
  - "Small commits"
  - "Green pipeline"
checks:
  - "Pipeline on push"
on_failure:
  - "Revert and review line by line"
  - "Split and merge in slices behind a flag"
rework: "Red pipeline → fix before the next task"
outputs:
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
handoff: "Commits on the branch (all tasks ticked) → 4.4.1 Open the Pull Request"
learning:
  - "Tasks that overran and why — learning log"
```

files.title: Subprocess 4.3.2 · Build in Small Commits on Trunk or Short-Lived Branches
files.body:
# Subprocess 4.3.2 · Build in Small Commits on Trunk or Short-Lived Branches

Turn the story into working, tested code through small, integrated steps that never leave main broken.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-2-code.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-2-run-code`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-3-2-code
title: "Build in Small Commits on Trunk or Short-Lived Branches"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/start-checklist.md"
  - "docs/task-breakdown.md"
  - "docs/repo-standards.md"
entry:
  - "Story kicked off; branch created"
runs:
  - unit: "4.3.2.1 Build a Task to Done"
    spec: workflows/build-4-3-2-1-build-task.md
    command: build-4-3-2-1-run-build-task
    gate: "Task done"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Pair members swap driver and navigator"
  - "Developer testing (4.5) runs with the code"
gate: "Code Complete"
decided_by: "Lane owner decides when tasks are done; tech lead settles standards questions."
criteria:
  - "Each commit small and named after its task"
  - "Tests for each criterion written"
  - "Main merged at least daily"
routes:
  forward: "→ 4.4 Review & Integration (all tasks done → In review)"
  rework: "Tests reveal a design issue → design query (4.3.4)"
  alternate: "Unfinished behaviour → merge dark behind a flag (4.3.3)"
  escalate: "Blocked > 1 day → delivery lead"
  stop: "Risk past tolerance (e.g. data corruption found) → halt and re-plan — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
handoff: "Commits on the branch → 4.4.1 Open the Pull Request"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.3.3.1 · Put Work behind a Flag
files.body:
# Workflow 4.3.3.1 · Put Work behind a Flag

Register a flag, build behind it with both states tested and enable it only in staging.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-3-1-flag-work.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-3-1-run-flag-work`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-3-3-1-flag-work
title: "Put Work behind a Flag"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
preconditions:
  - "Work exposed to users or spanning several days"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Decide if a flag is needed"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-1-s1-decide-if-a-flag-is-needed
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Flag or abstraction?"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Tech lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "Component swap → branch by abstraction instead": s1
  - id: s2
    do: "Register the flag with owner and removal date"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-1-s2-register-the-flag-with-owner-and-removal-date
    skills: [flag-lifecycle-management, twelve-factor-app]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/flag-register.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Cross-team flag → release manager": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Build behind the flag; test both states"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-1-s3-build-behind-the-flag-test-both-states
    skills: [dark-launching, kill-switch]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, reliability-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dev-test-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Off-path fails → fix": s3
      "Flag would hide unsafe writes → finish before merge": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Turn on in staging only"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-1-s4-turn-on-in-staging-only
    skills: [progressive-delivery]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/flag-register.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Flag Safe"
criteria:
  - "Registered"
  - "Both states tested"
checks:
  - "Flag register review"
on_failure:
  - "Add both-state tests in CI"
  - "Default off in code"
rework: "Off-path failure → fix and re-test"
outputs:
  - "docs/flag-register.md"
handoff: "Feature flag register entry → 4.4 Review & Integration; flag targeting → RELEASE"
learning:
  - "Flag-related defects — learning log"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.3.3.2 · Remove a Released Flag
files.body:
# Workflow 4.3.3.2 · Remove a Released Flag

Each sprint, remove release flags that are fully on, deleting the dead code path with them.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-3-2-retire-flag.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-3-2-run-retire-flag`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-3-3-2-retire-flag
title: "Remove a Released Flag"
owner: "Tech lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/flag-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Flag fully on or past its date"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "List flags fully on or past removal date"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-2-s1-list-flags-fully-on-or-past-removal-date
    skills: [flag-lifecycle-management]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/flag-register.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Overdue twice → tech lead": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "Fully rolled out and stable?"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Release manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "Not yet → set a new date": s1
  - id: s2
    do: "Remove the flag and the dead path"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-2-s2-remove-the-flag-and-the-dead-path
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Update register and runbook"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-3-2-s3-update-register-and-runbook
    skills: [kill-switch]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/flag-register.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Flag removed"
criteria:
  - "Flag gone from code and service"
checks:
  - "Register review"
on_failure:
  - "Restore from the previous build; re-check targeting"
rework: "Not stable → new removal date"
outputs:
  - "docs/flag-register.md"
handoff: "Updated feature flag register → 4.6.3 Write the Runbook"
learning:
  - "Flag age at removal — learning log"
```

files.title: Subprocess 4.3.3 · Hide Incomplete Work behind Feature Flags
files.body:
# Subprocess 4.3.3 · Hide Incomplete Work behind Feature Flags

Let the team merge to main continuously while deciding separately when users see the behaviour.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-3-feature-flags.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-3-run-feature-flags`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-3-3-feature-flags
title: "Hide Incomplete Work behind Feature Flags"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
entry:
  - "Story needs exposure control, or work spans more than a day"
runs:
  - unit: "4.3.3.1 Put Work behind a Flag"
    spec: workflows/build-4-3-3-1-flag-work.md
    command: build-4-3-3-1-run-flag-work
    gate: "Flag Safe"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "4.3.3.2 Remove a Released Flag"
    spec: workflows/build-4-3-3-2-retire-flag.md
    command: build-4-3-3-2-run-retire-flag
    gate: "Flag removed"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Flag creation alongside the first task"
gate: "Flag Safe"
decided_by: "Tech lead approves new flags; turning a flag on outside staging belongs to RELEASE."
criteria:
  - "Default off"
  - "Both states tested"
  - "Removal date set"
routes:
  forward: "→ 4.4 Review & Integration (merge dark)"
  rework: "Off-path breaks → fix before merge"
  alternate: "Component swap → branch by abstraction"
  escalate: "Flag needed across teams → release manager"
  stop: "Flag would hide unsafe behaviour (e.g. writes to the ERP) → don't merge; finish first — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/flag-register.md"
handoff: "Flag register entries → 4.4 Review & Integration; flag targeting → RELEASE"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.3.4.1 · Resolve a Design Deviation
files.body:
# Workflow 4.3.4.1 · Resolve a Design Deviation

Check the change against the architecture and ADRs; when they don't fit, raise a design query and apply a recorded decision.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-4-1-conform.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-4-1-run-conform`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-3-4-1-conform
title: "Resolve a Design Deviation"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/adr.md"
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
preconditions:
  - "Story in progress"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Run conformance checks on the change"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-4-1-s1-run-conformance-checks-on-the-change
    skills: [architecture-fitness-functions, architecture-conformance-check]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer, performance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/analysis-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Does the design fit what we found?"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Developer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "Fits → continue": s4
  - id: s2
    do: "Raise a design query with a proposal"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-4-1-s2-raise-a-design-query-with-a-proposal
    skills: [c4-model, ports-and-adapters]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/design-query.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Decide: conform, update ADR or new story"
    owner: "Architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-4-1-s3-decide-conform-update-adr-or-new-story
    skills: [decision-record]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer, security-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/adr-proposal.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Proposal incomplete → revise": s2
      "Changes scope or NFR → product owner / DESIGN": authority
      "Design flaw → stop story; DESIGN rework": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Apply the outcome in code and ADR"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-3-4-1-s4-apply-the-outcome-in-code-and-adr
    skills: [expand-and-contract, instrumentation-with-the-change]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Design Conformance"
criteria:
  - "Checks pass"
  - "Every deviation decided"
checks:
  - "Fitness functions"
  - "Review of ADR fit"
on_failure:
  - "Raise the query retroactively; update the ADR"
  - "Add the ADR change to the PR"
rework: "Incomplete proposal → revise"
outputs:
  - "docs/design-query.md"
  - "docs/adr-proposal.md"
  - "docs/migration-plan.md"
handoff: "Design query outcome & ADR revision → 4.4.2 Review against Criteria & Standards (and DESIGN on ADR change)"
learning:
  - "ADRs changed by build findings — learning log and DESIGN"
```

files.title: Subprocess 4.3.4 · Work to the Design & ADRs
files.body:
# Subprocess 4.3.4 · Work to the Design & ADRs

Keep the code and the decided design in step, so the system stays the one that was reviewed and its trade-offs stay deliberate.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-3-4-design-conformance.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-3-4-run-design-conformance`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-3-4-design-conformance
title: "Work to the Design & ADRs"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/adr.md"
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
entry:
  - "Story in progress"
runs:
  - unit: "4.3.4.1 Resolve a Design Deviation"
    spec: workflows/build-4-3-4-1-conform.md
    command: build-4-3-4-1-run-conform
    gate: "Design Conformance"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Conformance checks run in the pipeline alongside tests"
gate: "Design Conformance"
decided_by: "Architect decides ADR changes; product owner decides scope changes."
criteria:
  - "No dependency-rule breach"
  - "Required signals emitted"
  - "Migrations expand-and-contract"
routes:
  forward: "→ 4.4 Review & Integration"
  rework: "Code violates a rule → change the code"
  alternate: "Deviation accepted → ADR updated, code follows the new decision"
  escalate: "Deviation changes a quality attribute or scope → architect / product owner; maybe back to DESIGN"
  stop: "Design flaw makes the story unsafe to build → stop the story; DESIGN rework — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/design-query.md"
  - "docs/adr-proposal.md"
  - "docs/migration-plan.md"
handoff: "Design-query outcomes & ADR revisions → 4.4.2 Review (and DESIGN on ADR change)"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.4.1.1 · Open a Reviewable Pull Request
files.body:
# Workflow 4.4.1.1 · Open a Reviewable Pull Request

Rebase, self-review and open a small pull request whose description links the story, criteria, tests and CI run.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-4-1-1-open-pr.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-4-1-1-run-open-pr`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-4-1-1-open-pr
title: "Open a Reviewable Pull Request"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/commit-log.md"
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
preconditions:
  - "All tasks ticked"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Rebase on main and run all tests locally"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-1-1-s1-rebase-on-main-and-run-all-tests-locally
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dev-test-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Self-review the diff"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-1-1-s2-self-review-the-diff
    skills: [checklist-based-review]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Change no longer needed → close": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Write the description; link story, criteria, run"
    owner: "Developer"
```

# Workflow 4.4.2.1 · Review a Pull Request

Judge the change against its criteria, the design and standards; record findings at file and line and an explicit outcome.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-4-2-1-review.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-4-2-1-run-review`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-4-2-1-review
title: "Review a Pull Request"
owner: "Reviewer"
inputs:

  - "docs/adr.md"
preconditions:
  - "PR open and green"

  - id: s1
    do: "Read the story, criteria and ADRs"
    owner: "Reviewer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-2-1-s1-read-the-story-criteria-and-adrs
    skills: [code-review]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Read the diff in context; check tests map to criteria"
    owner: "Reviewer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, architecture-reviewer, data-reviewer]

    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Check standards, security and readability"
    owner: "Reviewer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-2-1-s3-check-standards-security-and-readability
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer, performance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/code-review-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Approve, changes or rework?"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 4.4.3.1 · Pass the Quality Gate

Run every automated analysis on the change, triage what it finds, and pass the gate on new code.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-4-3-1-quality-gate.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-4-3-1-run-quality-gate`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-4-3-1-quality-gate
title: "Pass the Quality Gate"
owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
inputs:
  - "docs/pull-request.md"
  - "docs/supply-chain-policy.md"
preconditions:
  - "PR open"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Run analysers, SAST, secret and dependency scans"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-3-1-s1-run-analysers-sast-secret-and-dependency-scans
    skills: [sast, secret-scanning]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/analysis-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Triage each new finding"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-3-1-s2-triage-each-new-finding
    skills: [software-composition-analysis]
    reviewers: [legal-reviewer, quality-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/analysis-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Real, false positive or no fix?"
    owner: "Security champion"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Security champion decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "High with no fix → security lead": authority
      "Design-level flaw → stop PR": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Fix on the branch or justify suppression"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-3-1-s3-fix-on-the-branch-or-justify-suppression
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/commit-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Re-run the gate"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-4-3-1-s4-re-run-the-gate
    skills: [quality-gates]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/analysis-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Still failing → triage again": s2

criteria:
  - "0 new critical/high"
  - "Coverage floor met"
checks:
  - "Triage of every finding"
on_failure:
  - "Reviewer rejects unjustified suppressions"
  - "Gate fails if any analyser did not run"
rework: "Still failing → triage again"
outputs:
  - "docs/analysis-report.md"
  - "docs/dependency-scan.md"
handoff: "Static analysis report & quality gate result → 4.4.4 Merge on Green & Build the Increment"
learning:
  - "Recurring finding types → coding standards — learning log"
```

Regenerate the API reference from the contract, add examples and version notes, and publish it with the build.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-6-2-1-api-docs.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-6-2-1-run-api-docs`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-6-2-1-api-docs
title: "Generate and Publish the API Reference"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/api-contract.md"
  - "docs/dev-test-report.md"
preconditions:
  - "Contract updated"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Update the contract for the change"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-2-1-s1-update-the-contract-for-the-change
    skills: [api-first-design]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/api-contract.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Should not be exposed → remove": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Generate the reference in the pipeline"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-2-1-s2-generate-the-reference-in-the-pipeline
    skills: [di-taxis]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/api-reference.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Add examples, errors and version notes"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-2-1-s3-add-examples-errors-and-version-notes
    skills: [specification-by-example]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, security-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/api-reference.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Breaking change?"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Tech lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Breaking → add a new version": s1
      "Breaking for other teams → release manager": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish with the build"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-2-1-s4-publish-with-the-build
    skills: [docs-linting]
    reviewers: [support-reviewer]
    output: "docs/api-reference.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "API Docs Published"
criteria:
  - "Generated"
  - "Examples present"
checks:
  - "Docs build"
  - "Contract tests"
on_failure:
  - "Regenerate from contract"
  - "Contract check fails the build"
rework: "Breaking → introduce a version and deprecation"
outputs:
  - "docs/api-reference.md"
handoff: "API reference → 4.6.4 Check the Definition of Done; consuming teams"
learning:
  - "Consumer questions after publishing — learning log"
```

# Subprocess 4.6.2 · Publish API Documentation

Let other teams and services use our API without asking us, from a reference that cannot drift from the code.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-6-2-api-docs.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-6-2-run-api-docs`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-6-2-api-docs
title: "Publish API Documentation"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/api-contract.md"
  - "docs/dev-test-report.md"
entry:
  - "API contract updated for the change"
runs:
  - unit: "4.6.2.1 Generate and Publish the API Reference"
    spec: workflows/build-4-6-2-1-api-docs.md
    command: build-4-6-2-1-run-api-docs
    gate: "API Docs Published"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead

  - "Generation runs in the pipeline with contract tests"
```

files.title: Workflow 4.6.3.1 · Write and Dry-Run the Runbook
files.body:
# Workflow 4.6.3.1 · Write and Dry-Run the Runbook

Turn the change's failure modes into alert actions, recovery and escalation, and prove them in a dry run on staging.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-6-3-1-runbook.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-6-3-1-run-runbook`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-6-3-1-runbook
title: "Write and Dry-Run the Runbook"
owner: "Developer"
inputs:
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/flag-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Alerts defined"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "List failure modes and their alerts"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-3-1-s1-list-failure-modes-and-their-alerts
    skills: [failure-mode-analysis]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, vendor-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/runbook.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Cannot be operated safely → operability work first": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Write the action for each alert and kill switch"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-3-1-s2-write-the-action-for-each-alert-and-kill-switch
    skills: [runbooks, actionable-alerts, kill-switch]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer, support-reviewer]
    output: "docs/runbook.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Dry-run on staging"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-3-1-s3-dry-run-on-staging
    skills: [runbook-dry-run]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/review-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Every step worked?"
    owner: "Operations engineer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Operations engineer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Step failed → fix runbook or system": s2
      "Operability rejected → tech lead": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish the runbook"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-3-1-s4-publish-the-runbook
    skills: [itil-4]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/runbook.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Runbook Tested"
criteria:
  - "Every alert has an action"
  - "Dry run passed"
checks:
  - "Operations review"
on_failure:
  - "Dry run required before Done"
  - "Tune or delete alerts nobody acts on"
rework: "Failed step → fix and re-run"
outputs:
  - "docs/runbook.md"
handoff: "Runbook → 4.6.4 Check the Definition of Done; RELEASE launch readiness and OPERATE"
learning:
  - "Runbook gaps found in incidents — OPERATE feeds back"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 4.6.4.1 · Check Done and Hand Off to VERIFY

Check each story against every DoD item with linked evidence about one build, then hand the increment to VERIFY.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-6-4-1-done.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-6-4-1-run-done`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-6-4-1-done
title: "Check Done and Hand Off to VERIFY"
owner: "Lane owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/build-record.md"
  - "docs/dev-test-report.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
  - "docs/tech-docs.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-done.md"
preconditions:
  - "Merged and Staged"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Link evidence for each DoD item"
    owner: "Lane owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-4-1-s1-link-evidence-for-each-dod-item
    skills: [traceability-matrix]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, security-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/dod-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Second person checks every link"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-4-1-s2-second-person-checks-every-link
    skills: [checklist-based-review]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dod-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Every item met for this build?"
    owner: "Delivery team"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Delivery team decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Item unmet → back to the owning process": s1
      "Dispute → tech lead / product owner": authority
      "Cannot be done this sprint → re-plan out": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Assemble the hand-off pack"
    owner: "Lane owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-4-1-s3-assemble-the-hand-off-pack
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/increment-handoff.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Hand to VERIFY"
    owner: "Lane owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-6-4-1-s4-hand-to-verify
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dod-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Definition of Done"
criteria:
  - "All items met"
  - "Links point at this build"
checks:
  - "Second-person check"
on_failure:
  - "Done is computed from links — refused without them"
  - "Re-run evidence against the current build"
rework: "Unmet item → back to the process that owns it (review, tests, docs)"
outputs:
  - "docs/dod-record.md"
  - "docs/increment-handoff.md"
handoff: "DoD record & increment hand-off pack → VERIFY (Act V)"
learning:
  - "DoD items most often unmet — retrospective and learning log"
```

# Subprocess 4.6.4 · Check the Definition of Done & Hand Off

Make 'done' a checked fact: every DoD item met with evidence, so VERIFY receives a releasable increment and nothing is 'done except…'.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-6-4-done.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-6-4-run-done`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: build-4-6-4-done
title: "Check the Definition of Done & Hand Off"
owner: "Lane owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/build-record.md"
  - "docs/staging-record.md"
  - "docs/dev-test-report.md"
  - "docs/tech-docs.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-done.md"
entry:

decided_by: "The team decides Done against the DoD; the state is computed from evidence, never asserted."
```

team.AGENTS.md:
# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act IV BUILD · Scale: Product team. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
BUILD is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## BUILD: Produce working, integrated, reviewed increments through a safe, evidence-producing pipeline — each one done against the Definition of Done and handed to VERIFY as one versioned build.
- **4.1 Environment & Pipeline Setup** — gate: Pipeline Ready. Produces: Environment catalogue, Pipeline definition, Repository standards, Secrets inventory, Supply-chain policy, SBOM, Provenance attestation.
- **4.2 Iteration Planning** — gate: Sprint Commitment. Produces: Capacity plan, Sprint goal, Iteration backlog, Task breakdown, Sprint commitment, Re-plan record, Sprint review notes, Sprint retrospective.
- **4.3 Implementation** — gate: Code Complete. Produces: Before-you-start checklist, Commit log, Feature flag register, Design query, Migration plan.
- **4.4 Review & Integration** — gate: Merged & Staged. Produces: Pull request, Code review record, Static analysis report, Build record, SBOM, Provenance attestation, Staging deployment record.
- **4.5 Developer Testing** — gate: Developer Tests Green. Produces: Criterion-to-test map, Unit test results, Integration test results, Contract test results, Coverage report, Flaky test log, Developer test evidence.
- **4.6 Technical Documentation** — gate: Definition of Done. Produces: Technical documentation, Changelog, API reference, Runbook, DoD record, Increment hand-off pack.
- Act gate: **Definition of Done** — decided by: The team decides Done against the DoD; the pipeline refuses what fails its gates; the product owner accepts re-plans; the architect owns ADR changes..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: STY → ENV → PIPE → SPR → TSK → PR → CR → BLD → SBOM → DOC → DOD → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `build-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Product team
Write for a product trio and a delivery team. Use our shared templates, make outputs ready to drop into the backlog or repository, and flag anything that needs the team's refinement.

# Guardrails & hooks — Build

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Product team
- Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
- Watch for: Each person's agent producing inconsistent artifacts — use the shared templates
- Watch for: Discovery and delivery drifting apart

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### BUILD
- Only Ready stories enter a sprint
- No merge to main on red
- Commitments change only by re-plan with a reason
- No secret in code, logs or agent prompts
- Supply-chain policy
- Repository standards and coding standards
- Agents work on branches; people approve and merge

- Accepted ADRs and NFRs

- Approved tools and runners

# Workflow 4.1.1.1 · Provision an Environment from Code

Define an environment in code, review its plan, apply it through the pipeline and record it in the catalogue.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-1-1-provision-env.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-1-1-run-provision-env`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-1-1-1-provision-env
title: "Provision an Environment from Code"
owner: "Platform engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
preconditions:
  - "Hosting account available"
  - "Data class of the environment agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "List the environments needed and their data class"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s1-list-the-environments-needed-and-their-data-class
    skills: [twelve-factor-app]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Write or update the IaC module"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s2-write-or-update-the-iac-module
    skills: [infrastructure-as-code, immutable-infrastructure, ephemeral-environments]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer, architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Quota or network blocked → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Plan and review the change"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s3-plan-and-review-the-change
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, vendor-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Plan as expected — nothing unexpected destroyed?"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Tech lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Unexpected change → fix the module": s2
      "Constraint unmeetable → back to DESIGN": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Apply through the pipeline"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s4-apply-through-the-pipeline
    skills: [gitops]
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act IV BUILD · Scale: Enterprise. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
BUILD is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## BUILD: Produce working, integrated, reviewed increments through a safe, evidence-producing pipeline — each one done against the Definition of Done and handed to VERIFY as one versioned build.
- **4.1 Environment & Pipeline Setup** — gate: Pipeline Ready. Produces: Environment catalogue, Pipeline definition, Repository standards, Secrets inventory, Supply-chain policy, SBOM, Provenance attestation.
- **4.2 Iteration Planning** — gate: Sprint Commitment. Produces: Capacity plan, Sprint goal, Iteration backlog, Task breakdown, Sprint commitment, Re-plan record, Sprint review notes, Sprint retrospective.
- **4.3 Implementation** — gate: Code Complete. Produces: Before-you-start checklist, Commit log, Feature flag register, Design query, Migration plan.
- **4.4 Review & Integration** — gate: Merged & Staged. Produces: Pull request, Code review record, Static analysis report, Build record, SBOM, Provenance attestation, Staging deployment record.
- **4.5 Developer Testing** — gate: Developer Tests Green. Produces: Criterion-to-test map, Unit test results, Integration test results, Contract test results, Coverage report, Flaky test log, Developer test evidence.
- **4.6 Technical Documentation** — gate: Definition of Done. Produces: Technical documentation, Changelog, API reference, Runbook, DoD record, Increment hand-off pack.
- Act gate: **Definition of Done** — decided by: The team decides Done against the DoD; the pipeline refuses what fails its gates; the product owner accepts re-plans; the architect owns ADR changes..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: STY → ENV → PIPE → SPR → TSK → PR → CR → BLD → SBOM → DOC → DOD → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `build-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Enterprise
Use formal language and our approved templates. Back every claim with a reference to its evidence for audit, flag compliance, security and privacy implications, name the approver for each decision, and keep confidential details out of anything meant for wider sharing.
Access: Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.

# Guardrails & hooks — Build

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Enterprise
- Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.
- Watch for: Pasting confidential or personal data into unapproved tools
- Watch for: Agent output in audited artifacts without a human reviewer named

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

# Workflow 4.1.1.1 · Provision an Environment from Code

Define an environment in code, review its plan, apply it through the pipeline and record it in the catalogue.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-1-1-provision-env.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-1-1-run-provision-env`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-1-1-1-provision-env
title: "Provision an Environment from Code"
owner: "Platform engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
preconditions:
  - "Hosting account available"
  - "Data class of the environment agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "List the environments needed and their data class"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s1-list-the-environments-needed-and-their-data-class
    skills: [twelve-factor-app]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Write or update the IaC module"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s2-write-or-update-the-iac-module
    skills: [infrastructure-as-code, immutable-infrastructure, ephemeral-environments]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer, architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Quota or network blocked → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Plan and review the change"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s3-plan-and-review-the-change
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, vendor-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Plan as expected — nothing unexpected destroyed?"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Tech lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Unexpected change → fix the module": s2
      "Constraint unmeetable → back to DESIGN": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Apply through the pipeline"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s4-apply-through-the-pipeline
    skills: [gitops]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Apply fails → re-plan": s3
  - id: s5
    do: "Record in the catalogue; schedule drift detection"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s5-record-in-the-catalogue-schedule-drift-detection
    skills: [drift-detection]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer]
    output: "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review
gate: "Environment Ready"
criteria:
  - "Defined in code"
  - "Data class stated"
  - "Applied by the pipeline"
checks:
  - "Second-person plan review"
  - "Drift detection scheduled"
on_failure:
  - "Re-plan and re-apply from the last good commit"
  - "Reconcile drift in code, then re-apply"
rework: "Plan shows unexpected changes → correct the module and re-plan"
outputs:
  - "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
  - "docs/iac-change.md"
handoff: "Environment catalogue & IaC change records → 4.1.2 Build the CI/CD Pipeline"
learning:
  - "Parity gaps that later hid a defect — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act IV BUILD · Scale: Platform. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
BUILD is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## BUILD: Produce working, integrated, reviewed increments through a safe, evidence-producing pipeline — each one done against the Definition of Done and handed to VERIFY as one versioned build.
- **4.1 Environment & Pipeline Setup** — gate: Pipeline Ready. Produces: Environment catalogue, Pipeline definition, Repository standards, Secrets inventory, Supply-chain policy, SBOM, Provenance attestation.
- **4.2 Iteration Planning** — gate: Sprint Commitment. Produces: Capacity plan, Sprint goal, Iteration backlog, Task breakdown, Sprint commitment, Re-plan record, Sprint review notes, Sprint retrospective.
- **4.3 Implementation** — gate: Code Complete. Produces: Before-you-start checklist, Commit log, Feature flag register, Design query, Migration plan.
- **4.4 Review & Integration** — gate: Merged & Staged. Produces: Pull request, Code review record, Static analysis report, Build record, SBOM, Provenance attestation, Staging deployment record.
- **4.5 Developer Testing** — gate: Developer Tests Green. Produces: Criterion-to-test map, Unit test results, Integration test results, Contract test results, Coverage report, Flaky test log, Developer test evidence.
- **4.6 Technical Documentation** — gate: Definition of Done. Produces: Technical documentation, Changelog, API reference, Runbook, DoD record, Increment hand-off pack.
- Act gate: **Definition of Done** — decided by: The team decides Done against the DoD; the pipeline refuses what fails its gates; the product owner accepts re-plans; the architect owns ADR changes..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: STY → ENV → PIPE → SPR → TSK → PR → CR → BLD → SBOM → DOC → DOD → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `build-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Platform
Treat other internal teams as the customers. Capture their needs as service or API contracts, and consider versioning, backward compatibility, self-service, documentation and adoption.
Access: Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.

# Guardrails & hooks — Build

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Platform
- Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.
- Watch for: Building what the platform team finds interesting, not what consumers need
- Watch for: Breaking changes without versioning

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### BUILD
- Only Ready stories enter a sprint
- No merge to main on red
- Commitments change only by re-plan with a reason
- No secret in code, logs or agent prompts
- Supply-chain policy
- Repository standards and coding standards
- Agents work on branches; people approve and merge
- Sprint length and capacity
- Pipeline time budget
- Accepted ADRs and NFRs

### 4.1 Environment & Pipeline Setup

- No unsigned artifact deployed
- No secret in code
- Supply-chain policy
- Information-security policy
- Approved tools and runners
- Hosting budget

### 4.1.1 Provision Environments with Infrastructure as Code

- Production data never copied to lower environments unmasked
- Environments follow the organisation's hosting and data-residency policy
- Hosting budget
- Data residency

### 4.1.2 Build the CI/CD Pipeline

- Gates fail, never warn and continue

- Approved tools only

### 4.1.3 Manage Secrets & Access

- Access management per the information-security policy
- Vendor key policies
- Information-security policy

### 4.1.4 Secure the Supply Chain
- No unpinned dependency
- No unsigned artifact deployed
- Open-source policy
- Vulnerability exceptions expire within 30 days
- Open-source policy
- Vendor SDK terms

### 4.2 Iteration Planning

- Agents propose; people accept
- Sustainable pace
- Retrospective every sprint
- Capacity
- Sprint length

### 4.2.1 Confirm Ready Stories & Capacity

- Retrospective every sprint

### 4.3 Implementation

- Main stays releasable
- Coding standards
- Agents work on branches only
- Accepted ADRs
- Committed criteria

### 4.3.1 Start from the Story & the Design

### 4.3.3 Hide Incomplete Work behind Feature Flags

### 4.4 Review & Integration

# Workflow 4.1.1.1 · Provision an Environment from Code

Define an environment in code, review its plan, apply it through the pipeline and record it in the catalogue.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/build-4-1-1-1-provision-env.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `build-4-1-1-1-run-provision-env`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: build-4-1-1-1-provision-env
title: "Provision an Environment from Code"
owner: "Platform engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
preconditions:
  - "Hosting account available"
  - "Data class of the environment agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "List the environments needed and their data class"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s1-list-the-environments-needed-and-their-data-class
    skills: [twelve-factor-app]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Write or update the IaC module"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s2-write-or-update-the-iac-module
    skills: [infrastructure-as-code, immutable-infrastructure, ephemeral-environments]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer, architecture-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Quota or network blocked → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Plan and review the change"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s3-plan-and-review-the-change
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, vendor-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Plan as expected — nothing unexpected destroyed?"
    owner: "Tech lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Tech lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Unexpected change → fix the module": s2
      "Constraint unmeetable → back to DESIGN": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Apply through the pipeline"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s4-apply-through-the-pipeline
    skills: [gitops]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/iac-change.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Apply fails → re-plan": s3
  - id: s5
    do: "Record in the catalogue; schedule drift detection"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: build-4-1-1-1-s5-record-in-the-catalogue-schedule-drift-detection
    skills: [drift-detection]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer]
    output: "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review
gate: "Environment Ready"
criteria:
  - "Defined in code"
  - "Data class stated"
  - "Applied by the pipeline"
checks:
  - "Second-person plan review"
  - "Drift detection scheduled"
on_failure:
  - "Re-plan and re-apply from the last good commit"
  - "Reconcile drift in code, then re-apply"
rework: "Plan shows unexpected changes → correct the module and re-plan"
outputs:
  - "docs/environment-catalogue.md"
  - "docs/iac-change.md"
handoff: "Environment catalogue & IaC change records → 4.1.2 Build the CI/CD Pipeline"
learning:
  - "Parity gaps that later hid a defect — learning log"
```
